steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The marketing mix (4Ps) combines Product, Price, Place, and Promotion into a coherent strategy. All elements must be consistent - a premium product at a budget price with limited availability and cheap advertising creates confusion.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Product: what is being sold, including features, quality, design, branding, packaging, and after-sales service. It must meet customer needs and be differentiated from competitors.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Price: must reflect the product's positioning and target market's willingness to pay. Premium products need premium prices; budget products need competitive prices. Pricing must also cover costs and generate profit.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Place: how and where the product is sold. Luxury goods are sold in exclusive outlets; everyday products need wide distribution. Online channels have changed place strategy for most businesses.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why all four elements of the marketing mix must be consistent, using an example. | Describe how the marketing mix might differ for a budget airline compared to a luxury airline. | Evaluate whether a business should adapt its marketing mix when entering a foreign market.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Consistency is essential because mixed signals confuse customers and damage the brand. Example: if a restaurant positions itself as fine dining (product: high-quality food), but charges fast-food pric | Budget airline: product = basic seat, no frills, charged for extras; price = low, competitive; place = online booking, secondary airports; promotion = price-led advertising, sales promotions, social m | Arguments for adaptation: different cultures have different preferences (McDonald's offers vegetarian-only outlets in India), local income levels require different pricing, distribution systems vary b

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always check that all 4Ps are ALIGNED in your answer - examiners look for this specifically. When discussing the marketing mix, use the word 'coherent' or 'consistent' to show AO3 analysis. Don't treat the 4Ps as independent - a change in one affects the others (e.g. raising price may require improved product quality or more premium promotion).
